headline: NHL contract grades: Red Wings lock down Alex DeBrincat at fair rate for top scorer
take:
The Athletic reports that its contract grades have the Red Wings locking down Alex DeBrincat at a fair rate for a top scorer, noting he has scored 111 goals in 252 games with Detroit.

The numbers so far this season back up the "top scorer" label without suggesting he is running hot. DeBrincat has 5 goals and 9 points in 8 games, against 4.1 expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances), so he is only 0.9 goals above what his shots would normally produce. That is a small gap, which says his production is mostly real. He is also driving play: DET controls 57 percent of the expected goals at 5-on-5 when he is on the ice, and the team's share of the chances is about 8 percentage points better with him than without him. For a Detroit team sitting at 3-3-2 with a 49.8 percent expected goals share overall, that matters. The Red Wings have been outscored by 7.6 goals relative to their chances, so DeBrincat is one of the clearer reasons the underlying results look better than the record.
